## San Isidro on a Lima sightseeing tour

San Isidro offers a different perspective on [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), away from its colonial center. One of the neighborhood's defining landmarks is the El Olivar olive grove. This green space forms part of the visit to the city's residential districts, offering a change of scenery after historic facades and grand squares.

Our [Lima tour: San Francisco, San Isidro, and Miraflores](/peru/lima/san-francisco-san-isidro-miraflores/) includes the olive grove, Country Club, and golf course in San Isidro. If this neighborhood is important to your exploration of the capital, look at these particular stops rather than relying on the general description "Lima sightseeing."

## What we see in the neighborhood

The El Olivar olive grove is one of San Isidro's well-known green areas. Here we introduce you to the residential side of Lima and its green spaces. After the monumental facades of the historic center, the trees and surrounding neighborhood offer a different view of the city.

We see the Country Club and golf course while exploring the district. Playing a round, taking a lesson with an instructor, or using club services requires separate arrangements. If golf is one of your interests, let us know in advance and we can discuss adding it as a separate activity to the sightseeing tour.

## How San Isidro connects with the center and Miraflores

We begin with [Lima's Main Square](/peru/place/plaza-mayor-lima/), the [cathedral](/peru/place/lima-cathedral/), and the San Francisco monastery. For more about the monastery stop, see our [selection of tours visiting San Francisco](/peru/san-francisco-monastery-lima/).

Next come San Isidro and [Miraflores](/peru/place/miraflores-lima/). In Miraflores, the route includes Central Park, City Hall, and shopping streets including Larco Avenue. This sequence brings together historic landmarks, residential neighborhoods, and everyday urban life. At the end of the excursion, we return to the hotel.

## When to choose this sightseeing tour

This itinerary works well if you want to see several different sides of Lima, including San Isidro, in a single excursion. If you would like a leisurely, independent walk through El Olivar, we should discuss the time available there separately: a general sightseeing tour divides the day between several stops.

On our [15-day four-country tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/), Lima sightseeing takes place on the morning of the final day. A return to the hotel and an airport transfer follow. If you book the excursion separately, we will agree on the date, guiding language, meeting point, and price in relation to your onward plans.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which San Isidro landmarks are included?

On [this Lima excursion](/peru/lima/san-francisco-san-isidro-miraflores/), you will see the olive grove, Country Club, and golf course.

### Is a round of golf included?

The itinerary includes sightseeing around the neighborhood, but no sporting activity is listed. A round of golf and club access terms must be arranged separately.

### Can I combine San Isidro and Miraflores?

Yes. Both neighborhoods are already included in this city tour, along with Lima's historic center and the return to the hotel.

lead: "This journey covers Peru's coast, the Nazca Desert, Arequipa, Colca Canyon, Lake Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu, and the Amazon rainforest near Puerto Maldonado. The most important considerations are altitude, long transfers, the pace of hotel changes, and domestic flights, which are priced separately from the main itinerary."
---

## 21 days in Peru: who is this grand cross-country journey for?

**This journey is for travelers who want to experience Peru's three major natural regions in one trip: the desert Pacific coast, the Andes, and the Amazon.** Over 21 days, the route runs from [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) through [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/), [Ica](/peru/place/ica/), Nazca, [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/), [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/), [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), and [Puerto Maldonado](/peru/place/puerto-maldonado/).

The three weeks are not intended for an extended stay at one resort. The program includes many overland transfers, regions at different elevations, visits to archaeological sites, trips to islands in the lake, and several days in tropical forest. Your priority should be **experiencing Peru's diversity**, rather than the convenience of staying at the same hotel throughout.

## Five sections of the journey and how they fit together

| Section | Main highlights |
|---|---|
| Lima–Nazca | Ocean, dunes, geoglyphs |
| Arequipa–Colca | Cities, volcanoes, canyon |
| Puno–Cusco | Titicaca and Inca heritage |
| Sacred Valley | Machu Picchu and terraces |
| Puerto Maldonado | Amazon forests and wildlife |

### The coast: Paracas, Ica, and Nazca

The first days are devoted to Lima, the Larco Museum, and the capital's architecture. The group then follows the ocean to [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/). Along the southern coast, the scenery changes quickly: arid desert reaches almost to the sea. The next stop is [Ica](/peru/place/ica/), featuring the Huacachina oasis, a dune-buggy ride, and sandboarding.

A flight over the geoglyphs is scheduled in the Nazca area. From the air, the size and arrangement of the figures are far easier to understand than from the ground. Flights depend on weather and the operating requirements of the carrier. If small aircraft or turbulence are difficult for you, discuss this part before purchasing the tour.

### The Andes: Arequipa, Colca Canyon, and Lake Titicaca

After the desert coast, the road leads to [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/). The program includes an introduction to the city and Santa Catalina Monastery. The next natural highlight is [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/), with high-altitude scenery and stops along the way. Conditions change considerably here: long road journeys now take place at substantial elevation.

A separate day around [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) is devoted to the [Uros floating islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) and [Taquile Island](/peru/place/taquile-island/). Cultural encounters here center on lakeside life and local traditions. The journey then continues toward Cusco along the Route of the Sun, stopping at historical sites.

### Cusco, Moray, Maras, and Machu Picchu

In [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the itinerary includes Qorikancha, the cathedral, and archaeological monuments. The route then passes through [Moray](/peru/place/moray/) and its circular agricultural terraces, [Maras](/peru/place/maras/) with its cascading salt pans, and the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/).

At [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), the group boards an Expedition-class train to [Aguas Calientes](/peru/place/aguas-calientes/). The next day is devoted to visiting [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and returning. Unlike a short itinerary, this trip allows travelers to see many other sites and landscapes before reaching the citadel, helping explain the significance of the Inca road network and agricultural system.

### The Amazon: forests near Puerto Maldonado

After the highlands comes a flight to [Puerto Maldonado](/peru/place/puerto-maldonado/) and accommodation at the Inkaterra Hacienda Concepción eco-lodge. Several days are devoted to rainforest walks, canopy suspension bridges, and bird and wildlife watching.

The itinerary also includes an excursion to [Tres Chimbadas Lake](/peru/place/tres-chimbadas-lake/), where travelers may have the chance to spot giant river otters and other aquatic wildlife. The presence of an animal species in the area does not guarantee a sighting during a particular excursion. Humidity, insects, and boat travel call for very different clothing and preparation than walking in the Andes.

## Altitude and physical exertion: preparing for 21 days

The biggest change in conditions comes between the coast and the high-altitude regions. Cusco stands above 3,300 m, and the roads across the plateau toward Colca and Puno reach even higher elevations. Even without technically challenging treks, long transfers and walking excursions can be tiring. Travelers with heart or lung conditions, or other health concerns affecting altitude tolerance, should discuss preparation with a doctor.

One advantage of the 21-day itinerary is that the country's regions are explored in sequence, with breaks between major stages. Nevertheless, **it is still an intensive tour**. Being comfortable on a short city excursion is not the same as handling three weeks of frequent travel.

For the coast and desert, pack sun and wind protection; for the Andes, warm layers and comfortable footwear; and for the Amazon, light long-sleeved clothing, a rain jacket, and insect repellent. Plan clothing for each region rather than trying to rely on a single outfit for all 21 days.

## When to travel and how to account for weather across regions

There is no single perfect season for the coast, mountain roads, and rainforest. Some months are more likely to bring dry weather in the Andes but cold mornings; others have more cloud and precipitation. The Amazon remains hot and humid, and walks and boat excursions depend on local conditions.

When choosing dates, identify **your main priority**: Machu Picchu, Andean landscapes seen from the road, wildlife watching, or experiencing all the regions together. Then check specific flights, train tickets, and the entry rules for archaeological sites. Machu Picchu admission is issued for a particular route and time slot, so the train journey and guided visit must be coordinated in advance.

## What is included and what costs extra?

The trip includes accommodation in 4-star hotels with breakfast, group excursions, and transfers. The main itinerary also specifies accommodation at an eco-lodge for the Amazon section; the final lodging and meal arrangements there should be checked against the confirmed travel option.

**International and domestic flights are paid for separately.** The itinerary gives a guideline of from $500 per person for domestic flights. Tips, personal spending, and optional expenses are also listed separately. This is important when comparing the trip with shorter tours, some of which may include flights in the package price.

If you cannot spend three weeks away, compare our [current Peru tours](/peru/tour/). Shorter routes let you see Machu Picchu and Cusco, but they do not offer the same combination of the Nazca Desert, a high-altitude lake, and several days in the Amazon. The appeal of this longer trip is the breadth of its geography.

## Frequently asked questions about the grand Peru tour

### How demanding is the trip without a multi-day trek?

It is not a trekking expedition, but it includes significant altitude, long transfers, guided excursions, and frequent hotel changes. Assess the exertion across the entire 21-day journey.

### How much time is spent in the Amazon?

The Amazon section begins on day 15 with a flight to Puerto Maldonado. Rainforest excursions and the lake visit continue until the return to Lima on day 19.

### How do travelers get to Machu Picchu?

An Expedition-class tourist train runs from Ollantaytambo to Aguas Calientes, followed by a visit to the citadel the next day. Admission tickets and the exact entry time need to be coordinated with the tour dates.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. The published itinerary lists domestic flights among the excluded expenses, with a guideline starting at $500 per person.

### Is the program suitable for a first visit to Peru?

Yes, if you have three weeks and are comfortable with frequent travel. For a first introduction with less time on the move, consider the [short Lima–Cusco–Machu Picchu itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-6-days/).

## All of Peru and Iquitos in 15 days: the Andes, the coast, and the Amazon

This itinerary brings together three very different natural and cultural regions: the coast around [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), the high Andes with [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), and the humid Amazon rainforest reached from [Iquitos](/peru/place/iquitos/). The journey lasts **15 days and 14 nights**. It suits travelers hoping to combine ancient sites and tropical forest wildlife in a single trip.

The greatest difference from a classic Peru itinerary is **the final section at an Amazon lodge near Iquitos**. Here the daily rhythm revolves around rainforest walks, boat trips, and wildlife observation. When selecting this trip, consider not only the number of cities but also accommodation and guiding arrangements during the Amazon section.

## Three stages of one journey

| Days | Places and activities |
|---|---|
| 1–5 | Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu |
| 6–10 | Titicaca, Colca, Arequipa |
| 11–15 | Lima, Iquitos, the Amazon |

The journey begins with [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) and Cusco's historic neighborhoods, then passes through the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Day six includes the journey from Cusco to Puno, while day seven is devoted to Lake Titicaca and the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/).

The road then continues through [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) and [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/), followed by a domestic flight back to Lima. Day eleven is free. If you wish, you can book a separate excursion to [Paracas, the Ballestas Islands, and a flight over the Nazca Lines](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/). **This is an optional excursion, not a mandatory part of the main itinerary.**

Day twelve begins with a flight to Iquitos, a transfer to the port, and a boat journey to the lodge. The following days focus on the Amazon and the return via Lima.

## Machu Picchu, Titicaca, and other Andean regions

The cultural section includes Inca archaeological sites, the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), and highland towns. An **Expedition-class** train ticket is listed among the included rail services. The exact sightseeing circuit at Machu Picchu is determined by the ticketing system; certain climbs and routes require the appropriate authorization.

After Cusco, the journey takes travelers into the highlands. Lake Titicaca and the roads of southern Peru are at considerable altitude, so preparation matters. A visit to the Uros Islands is scheduled on the lake before the route continues toward Colca and Arequipa.

This section offers more than a visit to a single archaeological center: it reveals how Inca complexes, colonial cities, mountain passes, and lakeside communities exist alongside one another.

## Traveling to Iquitos and the lodge

On **day twelve**, travelers fly from Lima to [Iquitos](/peru/place/iquitos/). After an airport welcome, they transfer to the port and continue **by boat along the Amazon River** to the Cumaceba lodge. Once settled, they have opportunities to observe the river and walk in the rainforest.

Day thirteen is devoted to Amazon excursions with **full board**. Activities include an early forest walk, piranha fishing, a visit to a Bora community, observing animals at a specialized facility, and searching for pink river dolphins. A nighttime canoe outing to look for caimans is also planned.

Sightings of dolphins, caimans, and other free-ranging animals depend on natural conditions. **The program provides the specified type of excursion, not a guarantee of seeing every species mentioned.** Travelers particularly interested in Amazon birds and mammals should clarify excursion times, observation arrangements, and rules for behaving near wildlife.

Day fourteen includes the return from Iquitos to Lima; the trip ends on day fifteen.

## How the Amazon differs from the Andean part of the tour

In cities and archaeological areas, much of the time is spent on land excursions, transfers, and train journeys. Around Iquitos, travel takes place on the river and forest trails. You will need a different set of belongings: light clothing that covers the skin, insect and rain protection, suitable shoes for wet surfaces, and waterproof protection for electronics.

The current list of services states that **excursions with a Russian-speaking interpreter are provided except in Iquitos**. The description therefore does not promise Russian-language assistance at the Amazon lodge. The language of the local guide and communication arrangements must be agreed separately.

This tour does not confirm a visit to a specific protected Amazon reserve. Being based in Iquitos does not automatically mean the group visits Pacaya-Samiria, for example. Choose on the basis of the river journeys and lodge excursions actually described.

## Included services and additional expenses

The tour price is **$3,910**. Included services list **domestic flights Lima–Cusco, Arequipa–Lima, and Lima–Iquitos–Lima**, an Expedition-class train ticket, the specified meals, and excursions with a Russian-speaking interpreter outside the Amazon section.

Excess baggage charges, alcoholic and soft drinks, tips, and excursions or options carrying separate prices are excluded. In particular, Paracas, the Ballestas Islands, and Nazca are offered as a possible addition on the free day, so they require a separate decision and budget.

Flights between regions add variety but require time for connections, luggage, and early departures. The program allows the order of excursions to change while preserving their content, and hotels may be replaced with properties of a comparable category.

If the Amazon is not essential, compare [other Peru tours](/peru/tour/) and the [eight-day "Ancestral Energy" itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-ancestral-energy/). If tropical nature is your priority, the [wildlife and nature travel section](/interests/wildlife/) is also relevant.

## Frequently asked questions about the "All of Peru and Iquitos" tour

### How many days do travelers spend in the Amazon?

The flight to Iquitos and arrival at the lodge are scheduled for day 12, rainforest excursions for day 13, and the return to Lima for day 14.

### Are domestic flights included?

Yes. Flights Lima–Cusco, Arequipa–Lima, and Lima–Iquitos–Lima are listed as included.

### Are sightings of pink dolphins guaranteed?

No. Seeing them is an aim of a wildlife excursion, but actual encounters with wild animals depend on river conditions.

### Can I visit the Nazca Lines?

The description offers an optional visit to Paracas, the Ballestas Islands, and a flight over the Nazca Lines on a free day. This is not a required included stage.

### Will there be a Russian-speaking guide in Iquitos?

A Russian-speaking interpreter is specified for excursions except those in Iquitos. The language of local guiding at the lodge is agreed separately.

## How the Peru tour with a stay in Tumbes works

The first days of this itinerary are packed with visits to ancient Inca sites and mountain regions, while the final section is devoted to the Pacific coast. Over **16 days**, the journey combines [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/), [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/), and [Tumbes](/peru/place/tumbes/).

One important feature is that the beach stay follows the sightseeing portion instead of being squeezed between brief stops. On day 12, travelers fly from Lima to Tumbes and transfer to a resort at Punta Sal. Days 13 and 14 are spent by the ocean without mandatory excursions, and on day 15 the group returns to Lima.

This option suits those who want to see Peru's principal historic sites and finish their trip with several relaxed days. Travelers who prefer a purely mountain-focused program may find the extra flight north less convenient than returning home directly after Arequipa.

## Why the mountain section comes before the beach

The route from Lima via Cusco and Puno involves major changes in altitude. In [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), travelers are more than 3,000 m above sea level, and Lake Titicaca is even higher. During the first days in the Andes, it is sensible to avoid unnecessary exertion and allow for acclimatization.

Travel between regions is already built into the itinerary: a domestic Lima–Cusco flight, the highland transfer to Puno, a visit to Colca, and the journey onward to Arequipa. After sightseeing in [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/), air travel via Lima takes the group to the coast. Clothing, temperature, and pace all change: early starts and mountain excursions give way to relaxation by the sea.

The beaches at Punta Sal in northern Peru have a warmer tropical climate than the Lima coast. Yet the seasons differ between the Andes and the coast: ideal weather for archaeological excursions does not necessarily mean perfect conditions on every beach. When planning dates, we will help assess the whole sequence, including the final stop.

## What is included in the main itinerary and what is optional?

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is part of the main itinerary, with a separate day devoted to the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/). A visit to the floating islands on [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) is scheduled before the group continues toward Colca and Arequipa.

A flight over the Nazca Lines and visits to other optional sites should not automatically be counted as included. On this itinerary, Nazca is offered as an optional extra. If it is a primary goal, clarify whether another day is required and how the flight to Tumbes would be affected.

The listed price includes domestic flights Lima–Cusco, Arequipa–Lima, and Lima–Tumbes–Lima; scheduled excursions with a Russian-speaking interpreter; meals as specified; and an Expedition-class train ticket. Check the main tour description for individual hotel and accommodation terms: the package contents matter when comparing other [Peru tours](/peru/tour/).

## Preparing for the change of climate

Pack for cool mountain mornings, bring sun protection for the highlands, and include light beach clothing. Comfortable shoes are important for archaeological sites; in Punta Sal, sun protection takes priority. Domestic airlines have carrier-specific baggage limits, so check suitcase weight and dimensions before departure.

Machu Picchu tickets are issued for particular circuits and time slots. Confirm availability in advance, especially when the entire schedule depends on connecting the train, guided visit, and subsequent transfers.

## Frequently asked questions about the Peru tour with Tumbes beaches

### How much time is spent at the beach?

On this 16-day itinerary, arrival in Tumbes is scheduled for day 12, days 13–14 are for relaxing beside the ocean, and day 15 brings the return to Lima.

### Do I need to buy domestic flights separately?

Flights Lima–Cusco, Arequipa–Lima, and Lima–Tumbes–Lima are listed among the included services. Check the tour conditions for international flights and final arrangements.

### Are all Nazca excursions included?

No. Nazca is among the additional options that need separate arrangements. The core itinerary centers on Inca history, Lake Titicaca, Colca Canyon, and coastal relaxation.

### How does this option differ from a beach-only Peru holiday?

The first part of the trip focuses on the cultural and natural attractions of the Andes. The beach is the conclusion to a longer journey; if you want an extended seaside stay, explore our [beach holidays](/interests/beach-holidays/) separately.

## How to compare Peru tours before booking

**First decide how much of your vacation you want to spend in each region.** A shorter itinerary may be enough to explore [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). If you also want [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), the Amazon, or time by the sea, choose a trip with separate days allocated to these destinations.

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Peru as part of the main itinerary. Some focus on Peru alone, while others continue into neighboring countries. The total length of a multi-country journey therefore tells you little about how much time will actually be spent in Peru.

| What you want from the trip | Where to start comparing |
|---|---|
| A short introduction | [Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-6-days/) |
| Add Lake Titicaca | [Peru in 8 days](/peru/tour/peru-8-days/) |
| The Andes and rainforest | [Peru and Iquitos](/peru/tour/peru-iquitos-discovery/) |
| A beach finale | [Peru and the beaches of Tumbes](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) |
| Special train and hotels | ["Inca Deluxe"](/peru/tour/peru-inca-deluxe-8-days/) |
| An extended journey | [The best of Peru in 21 days](/peru/tour/best-of-peru-21-days/) |

Our [Peru travel guide](/peru/) covers geography and seasons in more detail. When choosing a tour, focus instead on the number of nights, what is included in the total price, the class of transport, and which activities are actually covered.

## Short tours: what you pay for and how much time you have on location

The [six-day Lima, Cusco, and Machu Picchu tour](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-6-days/) suits a limited vacation or a standalone Peru segment within a longer trip. It includes an Expedition-class train ticket, guided visits, and assistance from a Russian-speaking guide.

[Peru in 8 days](/peru/tour/peru-8-days/) continues to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). Its included domestic flights are listed from [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and from Juliaca back to Lima. This makes a substantial difference to the budget: even two tours with an identical "from" price could entail very different expenses after purchase.

The main difference between shorter options is the additional geography. A longer program does not necessarily give you more free time in a city you already know. Check how the extra days are used: getting to the lake, taking an excursion, or resting.

The final day is especially important on a short itinerary. If the program finishes in one city but your international flight departs from another, you need to account for the connecting flight separately. Before paying, match the finishing city, airport, and transfer times with your own flight tickets.

Explore the history and available ways to visit important sites among our [cultural and historical Peru tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/). The key question here is whether the itinerary fits your time off and the services you expect.

## Included or optional excursion: how to read the itinerary

A place mentioned in a tour description may be an option for a free day. Its appearance on a page does not in itself mean it is included in the price. Look for wording such as "optional," "on request," and "at extra cost," as well as the list of excluded services.

A good example is the ["Enchanting Peru and Iquitos" tour](/peru/tour/peru-iquitos-discovery/). A visit to the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) is offered there as a separately paid option. If the valley is one of your priorities, add the excursion to your total budget and check which day it would occupy.

Our [separate Sacred Valley of the Incas excursion](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-of-the-incas-tour/) has its own itinerary. This helps you understand the activity, but whether it is included in a multi-day journey depends on that particular tour.

A free day can be more valuable than another compulsory excursion. It leaves room for walking, resting, or a suitable optional trip. But a full-day outing changes the timetable: account for early departure, return time, and the next flight.

| What the itinerary says | What to clarify |
|---|---|
| Free day | Which options cost extra |
| Train to Machu Picchu | Class, departure station, and time |
| Included meals | Which meals are covered |
| Guided services | Language on each leg |
| Domestic flights | Exact list of included tickets |

This approach is especially helpful with longer tours. A list of destinations gives you an overview; the day-by-day program and payment terms show what the journey will really cost.

## The Amazon, beaches, or a longer journey: which finale to choose?

[Peru and Iquitos](/peru/tour/peru-iquitos-discovery/) combines historical sites, [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), and the Amazon, including a lodge stay. A journey via [Iquitos](/peru/place/iquitos/) is suited to travelers who want river trips and tropical forest after the highlands. Domestic flights are included in this itinerary, so read their exact list before comparing the price with other options.

The rainforest section needs time for the flight, transfer to the lodge, and excursions themselves. Count the full days of activities between arrival and departure. Animal sightings depend on observation conditions; a photograph on the website is not a guarantee of encountering a particular species. More nature-focused options appear among our [Peru wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/peru/).

The ["Complete Peru and the Beaches of Tumbes" tour](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) is designed for a few tranquil days by the ocean after the sightseeing section. The route passes through [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/) and [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) before finishing on the [Tumbes](/peru/place/tumbes/) coast. If seaside rest is essential, compare the number of full beach days and the flights needed to get there. The first and last days in the resort area may partly be taken up by travel.

The ["Best of Peru in 21 Days" itinerary](/peru/tour/best-of-peru-21-days/) is for travelers ready to devote a long holiday to the country. It covers the coast, Andes, and Amazon. Parts of the route are overland, so driving time matters as much as the list of stops. Excursions and transfers are organized for groups, while domestic flights cost extra.

To decide between a lodge and a beach extension, picture the final days of your holiday. In the Amazon, you continue exploring nature. On the coast, there is more room for rest without constantly changing hotels. Both are worthwhile; the choice depends on how active you want to be after the Andes.

## Trains and accommodation: compare the actual services

The ["Inca Deluxe" tour](/peru/tour/peru-inca-deluxe-8-days/) differs from a short introductory trip in its transport and accommodation. It includes 5-star hotels and Hiram Bingham train tickets. A Russian-speaking guide is available on request, while Lima–Cusco–Lima domestic flights are excluded from the price.

Evaluate the higher price in relation to what matters to you. One traveler values a particular train and hotel, another prefers more days in an additional region. These criteria offer a more useful comparison than names such as "classic" and "luxury."

The [Machu Picchu Hiram Bingham excursion with tea](/peru/machu-picchu/machu-picchu-hiram-bingham-sanctuary-tea/) has its own description. On a multi-day journey, compare that experience with the actual day in your tour program: the precise service sequence and included activities belong to the chosen product.

A train ticket and entry to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) serve different purposes. Official visitor rules provide for several routes inside the complex. Before paying, confirm the agreed admission circuit and time slot and how they fit with trains and transfers. A premium train's name alone says nothing about the sightseeing circuit at the archaeological site.

For other higher-comfort options, explore [VIP tours in Peru](/vip/peru/). Accommodation, guiding language, and transport should be checked for every program separately.

## Peru and Bolivia: what does a cross-border extension add?

[Peru and Bolivia with Uyuni in 12 days](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) and [Peru, Uyuni, and the Altiplano lakes](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) are scheduled group itineraries. Both have departure dates in 2027 and a minimum group size of two participants. This changes the planning process: choose your holiday dates around the scheduled departure, then confirm spaces and tickets.

Some of the additional days on the longer itinerary are spent in Bolivia's natural areas. If your main aim is, for instance, more time in [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) or [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), an increase in the total tour length does not necessarily achieve it.

Certain sections have their own conditions. Russian-speaking guiding is excluded in the Titicaca and Uyuni areas. On the 15-day version, the La Paz–Lima flight costs extra. In the 12-day version, it appears on the route but is absent from the included flight list; its cost and inclusion should therefore be confirmed before payment.

To compare high-altitude and nature-focused sections, see our [adventure tours in Peru](/interests/adventure/tours/peru/). Other country combinations can be found in the [multi-country travel section](/multi-country/).

## Seasons and itinerary order: reviewing your chosen trip

Peru's official tourism portal describes approximately April to October as the lower-rainfall period for the Andes and Amazon, with November to March more likely to be rainy. This is a general guide when choosing dates: weather on any given day depends on the location and conditions. The coast has a different climate, so a beach finale needs to be evaluated separately from the mountain section.

On journeys through several high-altitude areas, look at the sequence of overnight stays and the exertion during the first days after ascent. Individual altitude tolerance is best discussed with a doctor before planning strenuous high-altitude activities. Ask for the exact sleeping altitudes and the duration of walking sections when choosing a tour.

Before buying international flight tickets, confirm the key [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) day, the included flights, and connecting transfers. For group departures, confirm the start date; for private travel, verify service availability on your chosen dates.

## Questions about choosing a Peru tour

### Is a short tour enough for a first visit?

The [six-day itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-6-days/) concentrates on [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). It suits a short vacation. If [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) is important to you, compare the [eight-day program](/peru/tour/peru-8-days/).

### Do all tours include domestic flights?

Inclusions vary. [Peru in 8 days](/peru/tour/peru-8-days/) lists included air tickets, while ["Inca Deluxe"](/peru/tour/peru-inca-deluxe-8-days/) lists the domestic flight among exclusions. Calculate the full budget only after checking these terms.

### Why is a visit to the same region priced differently in different itineraries?

Some tours include it as part of the main route; others offer it as an optional free-day activity. For example, the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) excursion costs extra on [Peru and Iquitos](/peru/tour/peru-iquitos-discovery/). Check the terms of the particular tour.

### Which program is best for relaxing after excursions?

The [Tumbes beach itinerary](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) includes time on the coast at the end of the journey. If you want to continue exploring nature, compare the [Iquitos and Amazon lodge option](/peru/tour/peru-iquitos-discovery/).

### Does a longer multi-country tour give you more time in Peru?

Some additional days are spent in neighboring countries. On the [15-day Uyuni and lakes itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/), the extension explores Bolivia's Altiplano. For deeper travel within Peru itself, compare the [longer country-wide journey](/peru/tour/best-of-peru-21-days/).
